task-intent.statement: The gate implemented a new write path into episodes/ inside scripts/mcp_spine_server.py, expected to pass the existing repo-wide test suite unmodified.

expected-behavior.statement: A new legitimate write path naming episodes/ was expected to ship without tripping any existing guard, since the write path itself was the change the mission called for.

observed-behavior.statement: tests/test_retirement_guard.py::test_canon_is_clean failed with 11 unapproved-store-mention violations the first time the full suite ran in a clean detached worktree. The guard held a FROZEN approval census (tests/data/store_mentions.approved.txt) of every site allowed to name the store, and a new write path had to be added to that census, with a reason per site, before the guard would pass again.

impact-cost.statement: One extra suite run and one extra commit were needed after the census was extended with 11 new entries and their reasons.

workaround.statement: The census was extended following the guard's own documented mechanism (a `# <reason>` line above each new `<path>:<normalized line>` entry), rather than editing the guard itself.

task-intent.statement: The merge-gate check ran the full suite in a clean detached worktree, expecting only the pre-approved MapTreeFreshnessTests failure.

expected-behavior.statement: A clean detached worktree of the branch was expected to isolate the suite from this session's own ambient process state.

observed-behavior.statement: tests/test_crew_launcher.py::ScratchDirResumeTests::test_resume_of_legacy_entry_without_worktree_key_does_not_crash_and_leaves_scratch_dir_unbound failed, asserting CREW_SCRATCH_DIR was absent from a launched subprocess's environment. This Commander's own process had CREW_SCRATCH_DIR set in its ambient environment, being itself a dispatched crew, and the test's fake-launch helper inherited the full ambient environment rather than a controlled subset. The same failure reproduced identically on the untouched base commit in a separate fresh detached worktree, with no code from this gate present at all.

impact-cost.statement: One extra investigation cycle (a second detached worktree at the base commit) was needed to separate a real regression from an environmental artifact before the merge-gate check could be trusted.

workaround.statement: The merge-gate check command was corrected, via the engine's own retext-check amend op, to unset CREW_SCRATCH_DIR alongside the SPINE_* variables it already excluded.

task-intent.statement: The design for automatically capturing a door refusal into episodes/ was checked against docs/EPISODE_STORE.md before being built.

expected-behavior.statement: The mission's own acceptance criterion (a refusal provable straight out of episodes/ from a single fresh-process trigger, with no separate agent-authored step) was expected to be achievable within the store's existing doctrine.

observed-behavior.statement: docs/EPISODE_STORE.md section 10 stated categorically that nothing should auto-create an episode, reasoning that an auto-created one could only carry fabricated assertions. This reads in real tension with the mission's own acceptance criterion, which required exactly an automatic, no-human-in-the-loop capture.

impact-cost.statement: The tension was not resolved locally: docs/EPISODE_STORE.md was fenced to a different lane for the wave this run belonged to, so the question of whether the categorical doctrine text permits this concrete design was left open rather than decided unilaterally.

workaround.statement: The shipped design made every captured field a literal quotation or extraction of data the refusal itself produced, never composed narrative, as a way of satisfying the doctrine's stated concern (fabricated assertions) without contradicting its categorical wording outright. The open question was recorded as a discrepancy and left for a wider-authority ruling.

task-intent.statement: A fresh cold critic, with no authoring context, was dispatched against the mission frame and the first candidate design for the capture mechanism, before any implementation began.

expected-behavior.statement: The first candidate design was believed workable going into the critic pass.

observed-behavior.statement: The critic found three defects that would have blocked the design at implementation time: the delta writer required a file path rather than inline JSON, a relative store-root argument was a cwd hazard in this module, and one of the five required assertion fields as originally scoped was still composed narrative rather than a literal quotation.

impact-cost.statement: All three findings were corrected in the design before any code was written, at the cost of one dispatched critic round before the implement gate began.

workaround.statement: The corrected design reused three existing module patterns directly rather than inventing new ones: a file-based delta-write shape already present in the module, an existing checkout-resolution helper for an absolute store-root, and the tool's own registered description text as a literal source for the previously-composed field.

task-intent.statement: This run's own feedback-step episode capture called episode_capture.mechanical_fields() directly, passing the worktree root as base_dir, matching how a first attempt at deriving a context-manifest-ref was made.

expected-behavior.statement: The function's own docstring described refusing rather than fabricating an unreadable field, so a missing context-manifest-ref was expected to mean no manifest existed for the step.

observed-behavior.statement: The context-manifest-ref field was silently absent from the mechanical bin even though a manifest file existed on disk for the step (.agent-work/567-e/context/feedback.json). The cause was base_dir: manifest_root() strips the work-id from base_dir's path to find the work area's root, and the worktree root passed did not end in the work-id ("567-e") and also carried no .agent-work ancestor, so the function's own refusal-not-guess branch returned None rather than raising past the caller.

impact-cost.statement: One extra investigation step (reading manifest_root's source) was needed to find the correct base_dir (the spine's own containing directory, .agent-work/567-e, matching what the door's own capture code already passes as SPINE.parent) before the mechanical bin could be completed.

workaround.statement: base_dir was set to the spine's own containing directory rather than the worktree root, after which the context-manifest-ref field resolved correctly.
